title: Proposal: `<toolbar>` element

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

While HTML generally does a good job of providing built-in equivalents of the various aria roles, there's still a number of gaps left. Like the [menu elements proposal](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11729) seeks to provide a HTML solution to the `menu` and `menubar` aria roles, it would be good for HTML to also provide a solution for the [toolbar role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/toolbar_role).

### What solutions exist today?

Currently you would have to use a custom element (or otherwise augment a div via JS) that provides all of the keyboard behaviours and sets the correct aria role. While the basics aren't too complicated there's a lot of complexity for effective conflict handling with the keyboard behaviour which is easy to get wrong.

### How would you solve it?

Over in OpenUI we're designing a new `<toolbar>` element ([explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/toolbar.explainer/)).

The TLDR is a new element which provides the necessary keyboard navigation behaviour expected for this pattern, and provides the aria role implicitly.

This builds off the work done as part of focusgroups, currently we propose utilising them under the hood but if focusgroups don't end up in standards for whatever reason I believe we can still utilise a lot of the work done and just not expose the entrypoint itself.

### Anything else?

As the goal is eventual inclusion in the HTML standard I'm opening this issue to start the wider discussion, there's still a number of unaswered questions that we plan to discuss in OpenUI and then in time with the wider standards bodies.
